class: A secret in the text a program reads, saves and passes on
symptom: The accessibility snapshot the agent reads carried what was typed into every box, password boxes included: it was written to output/<job>/pages/page_NN.txt (49 files), to the file the session brain reads, and, on runs that used the API, sent with every page.
site: any site with a sign-in or create-account form (seen on HonorHealth, Workday)
root_cause: safety.redact masks secrets in log lines only. The page text is a different channel (a file and a request), and nothing hid a secret box's value before it was saved or sent.
why_tests_missed: The redaction tests covered log lines; no test looked at what a snapshot of a page with a typed password contains.
fix: perception.hide_secrets replaces the value of a password, passcode, one-time-code or PIN box with [hidden] (inline value or the child text line a placeholder box draws, and the forensic tree). PageAgent.snapshot, the one place the page is read, applies it, so saving, planning and the forensic dump all get the hidden text. Saved snapshots were cleaned in place.
prevention: Redact at the one place a page is read, not in each place it is written. Treat every channel (log, file, request, dump) as needing its own check, and test each with a real typed secret.
